thread:
erin: Quick sync — I sketched a proposal to break session-manager into three smaller services: session-core, session-router, session-store. Thoughts on fragmentation vs keeping it monolith-y for the next 12 months?

david: Curious about the main goals. Is this to reduce dev friction, improve scaling, or pay down tech debt?
sara: All of the above? My read: session-manager is a hotpath for memory & kv pressure. Splitting could let us scale stores independently.
erin: Exactly. Primary goals: 1) isolate KV-heavy logic so we can try different storage backends; 2) reduce blast radius for deployments; 3) make room for per-tenant routing rules.
kai: Concern: operational overhead. Three services = 3 deployments, 3 SLA surfaces, more cross-service latency. Do we have metrics that justify split?
erin: We have telemetry showing tail latency correlated with KV contention spikes. I'll attach a tiny diagram in a sec.

-- code block --
services:
  session-core: handles auth, lifecycle, policy evaluation
  session-router: routes requests to tenant-specific backends, enriches routing metadata
  session-store: stores session state + KV caching layer

-- end code block --
sara: Nice. If session-store owns KV cache, we can try different eviction/quantization profiles without touching core logic. That is attractive for Optimize recommendations.
david: API compatibility is key. How do we version? gRPC with a stable contract or a facade proxy?
erin: Proposal: keep an internal facade for a 6–9mo strangler. session-core keeps the public API; router+store are behind it. We can route specific tenants to new paths via feature flags.
kai: Can we avoid synchronous hop on hotpath? Router calling store adds one network hop. Maybe co-locate router+core on hot machines and route only non-hot requests to store?
sara: Or use local LRU + async write-back to store for common cases. Want to ensure consistency model is clear.
david: Also think about tracing/observability: we need token-level cost and per-route latency breakdowns (console wants this). Make sure the console dashboards are wired before cutover.
erin: Agreed — onboarding telemetry is blocked until we map spans. I'll add tracing tags in the RFC.

infra-bot: reminder: there's an infra quota review next Thursday; any split that increases pod count will need an updated quota request.
kai: Good call. We should add estimated pod counts & GPU/CPU needs to the plan.
sara: For rollback strategy: canary by tenant, with automatic fallback to monolith if errors spike > 3% or P99 increases > 150ms.
erin: I'll draft a runbook for cutover + rollback tests. Target timeline: spike + small pilot over 6 weeks, broader rollout in next sprint if metrics are clean.
david: Tester/QA asks: need contract tests and an end-to-end harness that can run both monolith and stratified topology. I'll own the harness.
erin: thanks. Action items: Erin -> write RFC with service diagrams + telemetry plan; David -> contract/e2e harness; Sara -> storage experiments (eviction/async write-back); Kai -> infra cost estimate & quota ticket.
sara: One more ops thought: make session-store horizontally sharded by tenant ranges so we don't create cross-tenant hotspots.
kai: +1. Also include deployment cadence: independent releases for store & router, but core tied to facade compatibility.
erin: OK I'll post RFC draft tomorrow and link this thread. Any last quick takes?
david: Keep the API surface minimal for now. Avoid per-tenant feature flags that create combinatorial explosion.
sara: Agree. Start small, measure, then expand.
erin: sweet — thanks all :thumbsup:
